quarterly_data.signal: CFO David Weigand, outlook for Q1 fiscal year 2027: net sales $14.5 billion-$15.5 billion; GAAP diluted net income per share $0.89-$0.98 and non-GAAP $1.01-$1.10; gross margin 10.4%-10.8% 'Based on the expected customer and product mix'; GAAP operating expenses approximately $453 million, including approximately $127 million of stock-based compensation; other income and expense a net expense of approximately $45 million; GAAP tax rate 20.1% and non-GAAP 20.5%; fully diluted share count 745 million (GAAP) and 761 million (non-GAAP); capital expenditures $50 million-$60 million. Full fiscal year 2027 net sales $65 billion-$72 billion. CEO Charles Liang: 'I am very confident that fiscal 2027 will be our strong and fastest growth year again.'

CFO David Weigand on the revenue mix: for fiscal year 2026, enterprise and channel revenue grew 39% and represented 31% of total revenue, and OEM appliance and large data center revenue grew 104% and represented 69%. By geography, the U.S. represented 71% of Q4 revenue, Asia 11%, Europe 8% and the rest of the world 10%; year over year, U.S. revenue grew 259%, Asia decreased 15%, Europe increased 4% and the rest of the world increased 296%; quarter over quarter, the U.S. grew 12%, Asia decreased 13%, Europe increased 25% and the rest of the world increased 1%.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 enterprise & channel +39% (31% of revenue), OEM/large DC +104% (69%); U.S. 71% of Q4 revenue (+259% YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: Operating expenses (CFO David Weigand): Q4 GAAP operating expenses were $455 million; non-GAAP operating expenses were $357 million, up 49% year-over-year and 28% quarter-over-quarter, the increases primarily reflecting higher headcount related expenses and sales and marketing expenses. On the run rate: 'We think that the levels that we have are at the proper level. If you look at our historical growth rate in operating expenses, it is less than half of our revenue growth rate.'
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 non-GAAP opex $357M (+49% YoY, +28% QoQ); GAAP opex $455M

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Charles Liang on margin strategy: 'As you know, high volume GPU margin usually much lower. CPU, storage, IoT, enterprise application, on the other hand, have a higher margin. We will try to balance between the two vertical.' Looking forward, 'we will consistently growing our overall gross margin', and 'the DCBBS will be our long-term, much better profit margin product line.' On the FY2027 range of $65 billion to $72 billion: 'We like to support as many customers as we can, but the business has to be healthy. The margin has to be at a decent, meet the minimum financial kind of demand.' On the new orders: 'Overall, I believe our profit margin mix will be getting better.'

CFO David Weigand on the one-off parts of the Q4 gross margin: 'we did not book a tariff rebate in our numbers. We are actively pursuing refunds'; with the industry expecting that tariffs may go back up, 'that's why we still look at this as perhaps a one-time benefit. But time will tell.' Vendor rebates were 'a little bit higher' because of 'a different mix of business, more rebate-laden this past quarter.' Tariffs came down a lot in the quarter with the suspension of the IEEPA tariffs, and the good excess-and-obsolete inventory result 'was what we would consider a non-recurring event.'

CEO Charles Liang on funding the FY2027 plan and the upside: 'Once we take between $65 billion to $72 billion, I guess our cash flow now is pretty enough. But if there are chances to grow much higher revenue, then we may need more cash flow. For example, $80 billion or beyond $80 billion. There are some possibilities like that, but we will carefully control.' CFO David Weigand: the cash conversion cycle is expected to improve because the backlog carries improved terms - new customers came in and, with existing customers, 'we tightened the terms of those contracts' - which should allow the company to carry a greater volume of business.
quarterly_data.figure: CEO: $80 billion or beyond revenue among 'some possibilities'

players.product: GPU/CPU AI server and rack systems

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Charles Liang: growth momentum comes 'By expanding hundreds of new enterprise customers and other customers'. After many years fully focused on the GPU and AI market, the company is circling back to the enterprise CPU-based market, including enterprise, industrial PC, IoT and storage-based applications; in enterprise 'The profit margin is always better', and 'We are growing our sales force aggressively now.'

CEO Charles Liang on the GPU / CPU workload mix: in profit-margin terms 'the edge GPU is between traditional GPU and CPU'; 'Long-term GPU percentage will continue to grow, I believe. But again, lots of GPU will use in application, agentic AI, enterprise AI.' He expects the overall GPU market to be 'not just big, but also get into every vertical', and with DCBBS growing quickly, 'I believe we should be able to maintain the profit margin we plan for.'
